title: Geo-aware capacity fencing and fast-drain for multi-zone Dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Patel
description: Implement a geo-aware placement and fleet control subsystem for Dedicated capacity that enforces data residency at allocation time, provides throughput guarantees for reserved pools, and adds a fast-drain choreography for multi-zone failover with minimal token-loss and preserved KV-cache warmup behavior. This ticket covers control-plane policy, runtime allocation fencing, graceful fast-drain/soft-preempt, and measurable SLAs for cross-zone failover scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes placement policy with zone preference, hard-residency, and soft-stretch options
Provisioner rejects allocations that violate customer residency locks and records audit events
Throughput reservations can be declared per-pool and enforced with admission control under contention
Fast-drain sequence migrates queries to alternate zones with <= 200ms median additional latency and no more than 2% error spike in synthetic failover tests
KV-cache warmup hints preserved across failover: prefetch configured prefixes within 30s after failover
End-to-end integration tests in staging covering zone drain, region drain, and upgrade-without-loss run reliably in CI
tasks: Design and implement placement rule DSL in control plane (zone_preference|hard_residency|stretch) — proto + validation
Admission control: implement reservation tokens and per-pool throughput counters in allocator
Runtime: add 'fast-drain' signal that atomically switches routing policy and marks hosts as draining
KV-cache: persist warmup handles in allocator metadata and emit prefetch events to target zone on failover
Telemetry: Grafana dashboards and synthetic job for latency/error slopes during controlled drains
Security: extend audit log schema to include residency_lock_id on allocations
E2E tests: orchestrate multi-node synthetic workload and verify throughput SLOs under failover
Docs: API spec for placement policy and operator runbook for cross-zone failover
decisions: Prefer enforcing data residency at allocation time (control-plane rejection) rather than post-allocation tagging to avoid accidental egress

Implement two modes for multi-zone pools: 'region-local' (no cross-zone allocations) and 'stretch-soft' (prefer local, allow temporary cross-zone under explicit overcommit with customer opt-in), to balance availability and strict residency customers
Fast-drain will use an explicit two-phase handoff: immediate routing switch + background drain of in-flight KV cache writes. We rejected cold-cutover due to increased 95p latency and state loss risk
Throughput guarantees realized via token-bucket admission at allocator level plus soft-eviction policies for best-effort workloads — chosen to keep tail latencies predictable
We will not rely on global distributed consensus to make per-request placement decisions; instead use a placement decision with versioned leases and local caches to avoid added latency
risks: Cross-zone traffic for stretch-soft pools could increase egress costs unexpectedly if not surfaced to customers
KV-cache warmup may not reach steady-state quickly in high-churn workloads leading to transient quality regressions
Incorrectly implemented admission control could throttle reserved pools or starve burst traffic — requires thorough load testing
Audit/event volume for residency logs could increase retention cost; need sampling and TTL policy
Edge case: simultaneous region drain + autoscaler activity could oscillate allocations if not sequenced carefully
